summary: Defines a piece of the Management Information Base (MIB) for network management protocols. It extends the Ethernet-like interfaces MIB with objects for managing Power Sourcing Equipment (PSE), the devices that supply power over Ethernet cables. It is a proposed standard.

eli5.summary: Some network cables also carry electricity to power things like phones. This document is a list of dials and gauges that let a manager check and control the gear that sends that power.

subtitle: SNMP objects for monitoring and controlling the gear that sends power to devices over Ethernet cables.

tldr.problem: Ethernet IP phones and similar devices can be powered over the same cable that carries their data, but IEEE 802.3af defined only hardware registers for this, not a management interface.
tldr.mechanism: RFC 3621 defines a MIB module, POWER-ETHERNET-MIB, that extends the Ethernet-like Interfaces MIB with per-port, per-power-source and notification-control objects for Power Sourcing Equipment.
tldr.outcome: Managers can use SNMP to enable ports, set power priority, read detection status and power class, watch fault counters, and receive notifications about power state changes.

facts.label: Notification spacing
facts.value: At least 500 msec per object instance

today: RFC 3621 is a Proposed Standard from December 2003, and the metadata lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates it.

sections.title: Why a Power Ethernet MIB
sections.content:
IP telephony put voice traffic on the same infrastructure as data. That led to Ethernet IP phones, and with them the idea of powering the phone over the same cable used for its signals. The IEEE 802.3 Working Group began standardizing this as IEEE 802.3af.

IEEE 802.3af did not define a full management interface. It defined only the hardware registers that let a management interface be built. RFC 3621 fills that gap with a MIB module that extends the Ethernet-like Interfaces MIB (RFC 3635) with the objects needed to manage powered Ethernet devices and ports.

Two abbreviations from IEEE 802.3af are used throughout: PSE (Power Sourcing Equipment, the side that supplies power) and PD (Powered Device, the side that receives it).
sections.eli5: Phones that get their power through the network cable need someone to watch the power. This memo gives managers the switches and meters to do it.

sections.title: How the MIB Is Organized
sections.content:
The module is registered as powerEthernetMIB under mib-2 at number 105, and it is written in SMIv2, like other modern MIB modules. Its objects fall into three groups.

  • pethPsePortTable configures and describes individual ports on a PSE device. Examples of PSE devices are Ethernet switches that support power Ethernet and mid-span boxes.
  • pethMainPseObjects covers the main power source of a PSE device, such as the power supply in a switch.
  • pethNotificationControlTable controls whether the agent sends notifications to a management application.

The tables are indexed by a group and, for ports, a port. A group means a box in a stack or a module in a rack, and the value 1 MUST be used for non-modular devices. The same group value MUST be used in the port table, the main PSE table and the notification control table to refer to the same box or module.
sections.eli5: There are three boards of controls: one for each plug, one for the big power supply, and one that decides whether to send alerts.

sections.title: Per-Port Objects
sections.content:
Each row of pethPsePortTable describes one PSE port. The main read-write controls are:

  • pethPsePortAdminEnable: true means the interface can provide PSE functions; false means it acts as if it had no PSE function.
  • pethPsePortPowerPairs: signal(1) or spare(2), which pairs of wires carry power. It is writable only if the device can control its power pairs, as reported by pethPsePortPowerPairsControlAbility.
  • pethPsePortPowerPriority: critical(1), high(2) or low(3). A control mechanism can use it to avoid over-current situations by disconnecting lower-priority ports first. Ports for devices critical to the network, such as E911 telephones, should get a higher priority.
  • pethPsePortType: a string a manager sets to say what kind of powered device is attached. The default is a zero-length string.

The read-only status objects include pethPsePortDetectionStatus, which reports one of disabled(1), searching(2), deliveringPower(3), fault(4), test(5) or otherFault(6), tied to states of the IEEE 802.3af PSE state diagram. pethPsePortPowerClassifications reports class0(1) through class4(5), tagging devices by power consumption. It is valid only while the port is delivering power.

Five counters track events: MPS absent, invalid signature, power denied, overload and short. Each is incremented when the PSE state diagram reaches a particular state.
sections.eli5: Each plug has an on/off switch, a priority sticker, and gauges that say whether power is flowing and how often something went wrong.

sections.title: Main Power Source and Notifications
sections.content:
pethMainPseTable has one row per group and describes the main power supply. pethMainPsePower is the nominal power in Watts (1 to 65535), pethMainPseOperStatus is on(1), off(2) or faulty(3), and pethMainPseConsumptionPower is the measured usage in Watts. pethMainPseUsageThreshold is a read-write percentage (1 to 99) used to decide when to raise an alarm because measured power exceeds the threshold.

Three notifications are defined. pethPsePortOnOffNotification says whether a port is delivering power and SHOULD be sent on every status change except in the searching mode. pethMainPowerUsageOnNotification and pethMainPowerUsageOffNotification signal that usage went above or fell below the threshold. At least 500 msec must elapse between notifications emitted by the same object instance.

pethNotificationControlEnable switches notifications on or off for a group.
sections.eli5: The big power supply has a gauge and a warning light. If too much power is being used, it can ping the manager, but not more than twice a second.

sections.title: Conformance
sections.content:
The compliance statement pethCompliance makes three groups mandatory: the port group, the port notification group and the notification control group. The main PSE group and the main power notification group are mandatory only for PSE systems that implement a main power supply.

Read-write objects in the port, main PSE and notification control tables keep their values across a restart or reboot.
sections.eli5: Every device that claims to follow this memo must have the plug controls and alerts. The big-power-supply controls are required only if the device has one.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content:
Several objects are read-write, and unprotected SET operations can hurt network operations. Setting pethPsePortAdminEnable, pethPsePortPowerPairs, pethPsePortPowerPriority or pethPsePortType to wrong values can cause improper PSE operation, including a PD receiving no power. Wrong values for pethMainPseUsageThreshold or pethNotificationControlEnable can cause an excessive number of traps.

Some readable objects may also be sensitive, so access to GET and NOTIFY should be controlled. SNMP versions before SNMPv3 lacked adequate security. The RFC RECOMMENDS SNMPv3 with its cryptographic mechanisms, and says deploying earlier SNMP versions is NOT RECOMMENDED.
sections.eli5: If anyone could flip the power switches, phones could go dark. So only trusted people should be allowed to touch these controls.

items.label: disabled
items.desc: PSE state diagram is in the DISABLED state.

items.label: searching
items.desc: A state other than those listed for the other values.

items.label: deliveringPower
items.desc: POWER_ON for longer than tlim max.

items.label: fault
items.desc: PSE state diagram is in TEST_ERROR.

items.label: test
items.desc: PSE state diagram is in TEST_MODE.
